uncited: Analytic and Algebraic Methods convert continuous geometric primitives or parametric objects into discrete volumetric representations by evaluating exact mathematical properties (such as volume overlap or distance) rather than relying on rasterization or sampling.

It differs from [Rasterization-based Voxelization](11836-rasterization-and-projection.md) by computing exact geometric metrics instead of projected coverage, and from [Point Cloud Voxelization](1000-point-cloud-voxelization.md) by operating on continuous parametric definitions rather than discrete point sets.
All methods in this family map a continuous parametric object $Q_c$ into a digital representation $D_p$ defined on a 3D grid.
